litigation_timing.note: HCJ 9149/10 Wattad v. Knesset challenged the 2010 referendum statute (Law and Administration Ordinance, Cancellation of Application of Law, Jurisdiction and Administration, amendment of 22 Nov 2010) for setting a referendum requirement in an ordinary law rather than a Basic Law. The order nisi of November 2012 was outstanding when the Basic Law passed on 12 March 2014. The Basic Law put that same rule into a Basic Law, and the petition was later treated as moot. This was a pending petition on the rule the enactment changed, not a judgment the enactment responded to. The date of the mootness decision was not confirmed: the text extracted from the Sharf footnote shows '13.5.2014' next to the citation, but that date may belong to an adjacent citation of a committee protocol.

litigation_timing.note: Amendment No. 45 repealed s. 21A, the rule (dating from 2001) that ministerial regulations imposing criminal penalties need committee approval, with a tail clause deeming them approved if the committee does not decide within 45 days. The 4 July 2016 protocol says the repeal was prompted by a pending court proceeding on whether Fishing Ordinance regulations before the Economics Committee had been approved by default under that tail. The Knesset Legal Adviser had appeared in that proceeding with the court's leave and filed a position on 3 July 2016. The chair (Kish) said the matter 'is being heard in court today' and wanted a first reading so that 'the court will understand the direction'. The protocol does not name the court or give a docket number. Yes is coded on the inference that a challenge to ministerial regulations lies with the HCJ, supported by press references to SPNI's High Court petitions on the 2016 fishing regulations. It is not confirmed that the proceeding was in the Supreme Court or that it was still pending on 2 Aug 2016. No judgment preceded the enactment.
